scenarios.title: Stolen worker password
scenarios.description: One password-only route to synthetic care records; designed for an MFA-blocked comparison.

findings.title: Stolen worker password

controlEffects.reason: Require an additional authentication factor for a password-only transition.

findings.explanation: The simulated path is blocked at edge_worker_password_login. mfa/mfa_block_password_only at edge_worker_password_login: Require an additional authentication factor for a password-only transition.
findings.recommendation: Apply MFA to password-based access and verify that password-only transitions are removed.

scenarios.title: Shared workstation session exposure
scenarios.description: Two explicit alternatives: a stale shared session and a fresh shared session. Timeout matches only the stale route; individual-account enforcement matches both shared-identity routes.

findings.title: Shared workstation session exposure

controlEffects.reason: Replace shared-account access with individual identities, removing this modelled shared-account transition.
Expire a stale idle session; the rule does not match active-session tags.

findings.recommendation: Combine idle timeout with individual accounts; freshly active shared sessions remain after timeout alone.

scenarios.title: Former worker identity remains enabled

findings.title: Former worker identity remains enabled

scenarios.title: Excessive staff privilege
scenarios.description: A valid worker identity reaches payroll through an excessive role; normal identity access is a precondition, and the excessive entitlement is the defect.

findings.title: Excessive staff privilege

controlEffects.reason: A fresh authentication requirement reduces the modelled likelihood of the privileged operation.
Remove excessive or incorrectly assigned privileges from the synthetic identity.

findings.explanation: The simulated path is blocked at edge_worker_excessive_role. privileged_reauthentication/reauthenticate_privileged_operation at edge_excessive_admin_console: A fresh authentication requirement reduces the modelled likelihood of the privileged operation. rbac/rbac_remove_excessive_role at edge_worker_excessive_role: Remove excessive or incorrectly assigned privileges from the synthetic identity.
findings.recommendation: Enforce job-appropriate RBAC and require reauthentication for privileged operations.

scenarios.title: MFA social-engineering approval
scenarios.description: Assume a fictional user approves an attacker-initiated MFA event. The MFA control caps this human-mediated route to ordinal likelihood 2, while no session-token or password-only route is assumed.

findings.title: MFA social-engineering approval

controlEffects.reason: Additional authentication reduces this assumed human-mediated route without claiming complete prevention.

findings.explanation: The path remains; ordinal risk decreases from 16 to 8. mfa/mfa_cap_social_approval at edge_social_mfa_approval: Additional authentication reduces this assumed human-mediated route without claiming complete prevention.
findings.recommendation: Review MFA approval practices and strengthen verification; the model deliberately retains reduced residual risk.

scenarios.title: Compromised agency credential with authorised-operator alternative
scenarios.description: Primary route: compromised agency-password reference, a distinct password-authenticated identity context, a shared agency workstation, the scheduling application and limited synthetic agency data. Separate residual precondition: an already attacker-controlled authorised agency operator has completed required authentication and holds only necessary delegated permissions. MFA can remove the primary route while the residual route retains the same designed peak risk; these are design intentions, not observed results.

findings.title: Compromised agency credential with authorised-operator alternative
findings.explanation: The path remains with unchanged ordinal risk. No selected rule matches its transitions.
findings.recommendation: Use MFA for agency password access and review third-party assurance, delegated permissions and monitoring; retain the explicitly assumed authorised-operator residual route in the explanation.

findings.recommendation: Use MFA for agency password access and review third-party assurance, delegated permissions and monitoring; retain the explicitly assumed authorised-operator residual route in the explanation.

controlEffects.reason: Remove excessive or incorrectly assigned privileges from the synthetic identity.

scenarios.title: Multi-stage export with authorised-operator residual route
scenarios.description: Primary route: exposed service-password reference, service identity, service-support workstation, internal support application, excessive privilege, unrestricted export application and synthetic care archive. Separate residual precondition: an already compromised or malicious authorised support actor misuses a required export role. Privileged reauthentication caps the final operation, but the selected controls do not completely remove this legitimate-permission route.
